Title: Diagnosis of test `testGenerateURLFragment`
Details: The test `testGenerateURLFragment` checks whether HTML entities such as `"` are correctly escaped to their corresponding character by the `StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment` method. However, the test failure indicates that this is not the case. Following the execution path, we find that `StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment` is not escaping any HTML code; instead, it is using its input `toolTipText` as is. Consequently, un-escaped strings are being returned, which leads to the error demonstrated by the test.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

The failing test is in the method `winzipBackSlashWorkaround` in the test class `ZipArchiveInputStreamTest`. It attempts to read a zip file using the method `ZipArchiveInputStream.getNextZipEntry()` and expects that the entry name should have a forward slash `/` as a path separator. However, the actual entry name contains a backslash `\`.

The check that fails is the assertion on the entry name:
```java
assertEquals("\u00e4/", zae.getName());
```
where `\u00e4` is the character 'ä'. The test expects the entry name to be `"ä/"` but it is `"ä\"`.

Since the failure occurs in `ZipArchiveInputStream` reading zip entries, the root cause might be related to how the class `ZipArchiveInputStream` handles or normalizes path separators in zip entry names.

The methods that are covered by the failing test in `ZipArchiveInputStream` include the constructor and the method `getNextZipEntry()` which is responsible for reading and returning the next entry in the zip archive.

Next, I want to look at the code of `ZipArchiveInputStream.getNextZipEntry()` to understand how it handles zip entry names and whether it performs any kind of normalization or conversion of backslashes to forward slashes.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug.
